_meta.indication: To reduce the risk of hospitalization for worsening heart failure in patients with stable, symptomatic chronic heart failure with LVEF ≤ 35%, who are in sinus rhythm with resting heart rate ≥ 70 bpm and either are on maximally tolerated doses of beta-blockers or have a contraindication to beta-blocker use

pivotal_trials.trial_name: SHIFT (Systolic Heart failure treatment with the I_f inhibitor ivabradine Trial)
pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed FDA documents
pivotal_trials.phase: Outcome study supporting the HF indication
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial comparing Corlanor and placebo
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with stable NYHA class II to IV heart failure, LVEF ≤ 35%, resting heart rate ≥ 70 bpm; coronary artery disease was the underlying cause in 68% of patients
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Composite of the first occurrence of either hospitalization for worsening heart failure or cardiovascular death
pivotal_trials.n: 6558 adult patients; primary analysis arms N = 3241 Corlanor and N = 3264 placebo
pivotal_trials.result: Corlanor reduced the primary composite of HF hospitalization or CV death (hazard ratio 0.82, 95% CI 0.75, 0.90, p < 0.0001); the benefit reflected only reduced HF hospitalization (HR 0.74, 95% CI 0.66, 0.83) with no statistically significant effect on cardiovascular death (HR 0.91, 95% CI 0.80, 1.03)

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions in SHIFT (≥1% higher than placebo): bradycardia (10% vs 2.2%), hypertension/blood pressure increased (8.9% vs 7.8%), atrial fibrillation (8.3% vs 6.6%), and phosphenes/visual brightness (2.8% vs 0.5%); Corlanor also increases the risk of atrial fibrillation
target_moa: Hyperpolarization-activated cyclic nucleotide-gated (HCN) channel blocker that reduces spontaneous pacemaker activity of the cardiac sinus node by selectively inhibiting the I_f current, lowering heart rate with no effect on ventricular repolarization or myocardial contractility

advisory_committee.vote: Not referred to an FDA advisory committee because the application did not raise significant safety or efficacy issues that were unexpected for a drug of this class or in the intended population, and outside expertise was not necessary; there were no controversial issues that would benefit from advisory committee discussion

summary.text: Ivabradine (Corlanor) was reviewed under a granted priority review and approved first cycle on April 15, 2015, based on the single outcome study SHIFT; it was not referred to an advisory committee and the pediatric study requirement was waived.
